Class PlatformGateway

java.lang.Object
de.hallerweb.enterprise.prioritize.service.process.PlatformGateway
@Service public class PlatformGateway extends Object
The inbound facade: the one narrow place through which a BPMN process invokes platform operations — create a task, store a document, control a resource — under a single, defined system identity instead of through three scattered back doors.

Why one facade. Each of these operations already exists, but bound to a logged-in user because it was built for humans. A process has no user, so without this facade every delegate would reach for its own trusted path, and the system identity — and its limits — would be defined in three places or nowhere. Here it is defined once: the acting principal is SystemIdentityProvider, and what a process may do is whatever that principal is allowed to do.

Orchestration, not ownership (the line held throughout the Flowable work): the facade lets a process start work and record results; it never becomes the owner of a task's lifecycle. Remove Flowable and none of these operations lose their non-facade, user-driven form.

How a BPMN process reaches it. This class is a Spring bean named platformGateway, so a service task invokes it directly by expression — no per-operation delegate class is needed, the facade itself is the delegate surface: 

<serviceTask id="create"
    flowable:expression="${platformGateway.createTask(projectId, 'Round', 'inspect', 2)}"/>
where projectId is a process variable the platform set at start (see ProcessInstanceService).

  • Method Details

    • createTask

      @Transactional public Task createTask(Long projectId, String name, String description, int priority)
      Creates a task on a project's blackboard on behalf of the platform.

      This is a trusted path with no membership check — the caller is the engine acting as the system principal, not a user working on the project, the same shape as the scheduler's TaskService.createScheduledTask(Project, String, String, int). The task is attributed to the system identity.

      Parameters:
      projectId - the owning project's id
      name - the task's name
      description - the task's description
      priority - the task's priority
      Returns:
      the persisted task
      Throws:
      NoSuchElementException - if no project has that id

    • storeDocument

      @Transactional public DocumentInfo storeDocument(String name, Long groupId, byte[] content, String mimeType)
      Stores a new document in a document group on behalf of the platform — the trusted inbound path a BPMN process uses to record a result (a report, an acknowledgement, a snapshot).

      The document is authored by the system principal: lastModifiedBy carries the platform's own identity, so "who produced this?" has a real, queryable answer rather than a null. The document is versioned by the Documents subsystem like any other, and what goes inside it (PDF rendering, templates) is a vertical's concern, not the platform's.

      Parameters:
      name - the document's name; an extension is derived from mimeType if absent
      groupId - the target document group's id
      content - the raw bytes of the first version
      mimeType - the content's MIME type
      Returns:
      the created document
      Throws:
      NoSuchElementException - if no document group has that id

    • controlResource

      @Transactional public void controlResource(Long resourceId, String command, String param, int slot)
      Sends a control command to a resource on behalf of the platform — the trusted inbound path a BPMN process uses to switch an aggregate on or off, set a value, and so on.

      A process holds no reservation, so the target slot is supplied explicitly (0 for a single-slot resource). The command is refused (409) if that slot currently holds an active reservation, so a process can never seize a human's reserved control window. Permission is checked against the system principal (resource READ to load it, UPDATE to control it), so what a process may control is a checked property of the platform's own identity.

      Parameters:
      resourceId - the target resource's id
      command - the command identifier
      param - optional free parameter (may be null)
      slot - the slot to address
      Throws:
      NoSuchElementException - if no resource has that id
      org.springframework.security.access.AccessDeniedException - if the system principal may not control it
      SlotOccupiedException - if the slot is reserved
